race_context: Jay School Corporation serves Jay County (including Portland, Dunkirk and Redkey) and a part of Blackford County; Blackford voters who live in the corporation vote in the Jay board races {hcnt_ev}{cr_stadium}. State enrollment counts were 3,004 students in 2025-26, 2,950 in 2024-25 and 2,987 in 2023-24 {idoe_enroll}. The district's year-end report put enrollment at 2,905, up from 2,817 the year before {cr_yearend}.

The board has seven members: as of 2026, Ron Laux (president), Donna Geesaman (vice president), Marcie Vormohr (secretary), Chip Phillips, Chad Towell, Aaron Clark and Jon Eads {cr_yearend}{cr_budget}. Seats are designated by numbered districts {cr_0620}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: District 2, held by Chip Phillips, is open; Desi Brown and Tom Crouch filed for it, and Phillips is not on the ballot. District 3 incumbent Donna Geesaman faces Kendra McLaughlin. District 5 incumbent Ron Laux is unopposed. One seat each, matching the state list {cr_0620}{cr_0602}{in_list}.

A fourth seat, District 1 (held by Marcie Vormohr), was also up in 2026, but no candidate filed for it by the June 18 deadline, so it does not appear on the ballot {cr_0620}{cr_0530}. This guide did not find how that seat will be filled.

Party labels: 2026 is the first school board election in which candidates could declare a party. Crouch, McLaughlin and Laux filed as Republicans; Brown and Geesaman did not declare a party {hcnt_ev}{ic_list}.

Budget: the district's education fund ended 2025 at a record $8.32 million and the operation fund at $7.62 million; the rainy day fund was $1.82 million (January 2026) {cr_yearend}. In August 2026 the board voted to advertise a proposed 2027 budget of $44.2 million, up about 4.75% from $42.19 million for 2026, with a hearing set for Aug. 17 and adoption planned for Sept. 21 {cr_budget}.

Property-tax law (SEA 1): The Commercial Review reported that an August 2025 Baker Tilly presentation estimated that the 2025 tax-law changes would cost the corporation more than $500,000 a year {cr_yearend}. No operating or safety referendum was found.

Employee costs: in August 2026 the board stayed with its health insurer despite an overall premium increase of nearly $600,000 (about 14%), and raised the district's annual contribution to $9,120 for single plans and $19,608 for family plans; changes to teacher contributions go through bargaining with the Jay Classroom Teachers Association {cr_budget}. In April 2026 it approved a child care tuition-assistance pilot for employees capped at $150,000 {cr_stadium}.

Enrollment and school choice: a virtual academy pilot for grades 7-12, approved in February 2025, served 67 students in spring 2026; the district reported that students leaving for outside virtual schools fell from 119 in 2024 to 73 in 2025 {cr_virtual}. The 2025 graduation rate was 95.4%, about 7 points higher than the year before {cr_virtual}.

Facilities: in April 2026 the board awarded a $554,877 contract to repair and seal the Schutz Memorial Stadium grandstand, one phase of a larger effort that includes tennis courts, a band and choir room, electrical and heating/cooling upgrades and kitchen work; Gulley said the aim was to keep the stadium usable through the next bond cycle, projected for 2033 {cr_stadium}. Repairs from a September 2024 tornado that hit the junior-high wing had cost nearly $5.9 million as of January 2026 {cr_virtual}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum or questionnaire for the Jay races. The district website could not be loaded.
